intro: Find out exactly how much water you should drink each day based on your weight, activity level and climate. Stay optimally hydrated.

result.tip: Drink more if you're sweating heavily, breastfeeding, or feel thirsty.

formula.title: How Daily Water Intake Is Calculated
formula.explanation: Base recommendation: 35 ml per kg of body weight. Activity and climate multipliers increase this. Hot climates add approximately 500 ml. Heavy exercise adds 500–1000 ml on workout days.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: How much water should I drink per day?
faq.a1: General guidelines suggest about 2–3 litres per day for adults, but individual needs vary widely based on body size, activity, climate and diet.
faq.q2: Does coffee count toward daily water intake?
faq.a2: Yes. Despite mild diuretic effects, caffeinated beverages still contribute to overall fluid intake. However, plain water is the best choice for hydration.
faq.q3: Can I drink too much water?
faq.a3: Overhydration (hyponatremia) is rare but possible, mainly in endurance athletes who drink large volumes of plain water without replacing electrolytes. In normal daily life, healthy kidneys handle excess water efficiently.
faq.a4: Mild dehydration signs include thirst, dark urine, headache, fatigue and reduced concentration. Severe dehydration requires medical attention.
faq.q5: Does eating fruits and vegetables count?
faq.a5: Yes. Around 20% of daily water intake comes from food. Fruits and vegetables with high water content (cucumber, watermelon, lettuce) contribute significantly.
